callback_gas_limit.description: Gas limit on each nois callback submessage. Default 500_000.

prices.description: Accepted fees. Empty or omitted means requests are free (funds are still accepted).

pubkey.description: Compressed drand group public key. 48 bytes for chained, 96 bytes for quicknet.

required_attestations.description: Attestations required before a round can be delivered. Default 0 (drand only).

DrandScheme.description:
Drand signature scheme configured for this beacon instance.

JSON uses the scheme id published by drand (`/info` field `schemeID`). The ids contain `-`, which the `cw_serde` schema derive cannot name, so this enum derives serde and schemars directly and reports a string schema.

oneOf.description: League of Entropy mainnet "default". Public key is 48-byte G1. Signature is 96-byte G2 and is chained to the previous round's signature.
Quicknet. Public key is 96-byte G2. Signature is 48-byte G1. `previous_signature` must be omitted.

HexBinary.description:
This is a wrapper around Vec<u8> to add hex de/serialization with serde. It also adds some helper methods to help encode inline.

This is similar to `cosmwasm_std::Binary` but uses hex. See also <https://github.com/CosmWasm/cosmwasm/blob/main/docs/MESSAGE_TYPES.md>.

Timestamp.description:
A point in time in nanosecond precision.

This type can represent times from 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z to 2554-07-21T23:34:33Z.

## Examples

``` # use cosmwasm_std::Timestamp; let ts = Timestamp::from_nanos(1_000_000_202); assert_eq!(ts.nanos(), 1_000_000_202); assert_eq!(ts.seconds(), 1); assert_eq!(ts.subsec_nanos(), 202);

let ts = ts.plus_seconds(2); assert_eq!(ts.nanos(), 3_000_000_202); assert_eq!(ts.seconds(), 3); assert_eq!(ts.subsec_nanos(), 202); ```

Uint256.description:
An implementation of u256 that is using strings for JSON encoding/decoding, such that the full u256 range can be used for clients that convert JSON numbers to floats, like JavaScript and jq.

# Examples

Use `new` to create instances out of u128, `from` for other primitive uint types or `from_be_bytes` to provide big endian bytes:

``` # use cosmwasm_std::Uint256; let a = Uint256::new(258u128); let b = Uint256::from(258u16); let c = Uint256::from_be_bytes([ 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 1u8, 2u8, ]); assert_eq!(a, b); assert_eq!(a, c); ```

Uint64.description:
A thin wrapper around u64 that is using strings for JSON encoding/decoding, such that the full u64 range can be used for clients that convert JSON numbers to floats, like JavaScript and jq.

# Examples

Use `from` to create instances of this and `u64` to get the value out:

``` # use cosmwasm_std::Uint64; let a = Uint64::from(42u64); assert_eq!(a.u64(), 42);

let b = Uint64::from(70u32); assert_eq!(b.u64(), 70); ```

oneOf.description:
Verify a drand beacon and store `sha256(signature)` as the round randomness.

`previous_signature` is required for [`DrandScheme::PedersenBlsChained`] unless round-1 is already stored. It must be omitted for quicknet.

Attest a stored drand round. The signer must be a registered attestor.

Message is documented in the crate README and [`crate::attestor`].

prices.description: `Some` replaces the price list. An empty list makes requests free.

amount.description: Omit to withdraw the full balance of `denom`.

oneOf.description: Deliver up to the per-tx callback batch. Permissionless.

Pull entrypoint for `nftfi-raffle` (`RandomnessSourceMsg::Callback`).

The sender is the raffle contract. The beacon reads raffle `raffle_id` from the sender, takes the first drand round published strictly after the raffle end (`start + duration`), and answers with the attributes the raffle reply reads: `raffle_id`, `round`, `randomness` (base64, 32 bytes) and `owner`. Fails when that round is not stored or not yet deliverable under `required_attestations`.

BeaconSource.description:
Where a beacon value came from.

Verified drand outputs are stored under [`BeaconSource::Drand`]. Attestor signatures over a drand output are stored under [`BeaconSource::Attestor`]. Both are keyed by source id plus round (attestations also include the attestor key).

[`RESERVED_IBC_SOURCE_ID`] is the id a future IBC v2 client should use when a hash-market runtime starts aggregating beacons. That client should verify the packet, then write the same [`crate::state::StoredBeacon`] record the drand path writes. There is no IBC entry point in this contract.
